For most of history, money was private by default.

01 · Cash

No record

No one could look up what you paid, who you paid, or what you had left.

02 · Banks

Every payment, a record

Money went digital. Banks kept the ledger; at least it stayed behind their walls.

03 · Public chains

Readable by anyone

Crypto promised to give money back to people. Instead it built the most transparent ledger in history.

That isn't freedom. It's a glass house.

Every balance, every payment, every counterparty: public and permanent. On a public chain, all of it is one search away, forever.

  • Your salary
  • Your savings
  • Who you support
  • Who you do business with

We'd never accept this anywhere else.

Letters come in envelopes.

Medical records stay confidential.

Nobody prints your bank statement in the newspaper.

Why should money be the one thing everyone can read?

Privacy isn't about having something to hide. It's about having a life that's yours.

Public by default was a mistake.
Private by default is the fix.

404. Live on BNB Smart Chain.

                404

                The native privacy protocol on BNB Smart Chain. What you hold, receive and send lives in private notes that only your wallet can open.

                Replica notice. 404 is a BNB Smart Chain privacy protocol for private notes and authorized transactions.

                How it fits together

                Everything private sits in one pool contract. Instead of balances, the pool keeps a tree of notes. Each note is stored as a commitment: a hash that hides its owner, asset and amount. To spend notes, your browser makes a zero-knowledge proof. A connected public wallet can submit it and pays only network gas, or you can export the fixed proof as an authorization package for another device.

                Public wallet ──mint / deposit──▶ Pool ──▶ notes for your private address
                                  │
Your browser ──proof/package──▶ Public wallet ──▶ spend notes, create new ones
                                  │
                       withdraw ──▶ public {token} or BNB

                What you can do

                ActionWhat happens
                MintMint one free lot into private notes; the submitting wallet pays network gas. Older paid pools display their configured on-chain price.
                SendPay any 4041 address in {token} or BNB. Sender, recipient and amount stay hidden.
                Deposit / WithdrawMove funds between a public wallet and your private balance.
                MarketList, offer and fill limit orders without showing who trades.

                Key numbers

                Supply21,000,000 {token} in 21,000 lots
                Mint priceFree

                Submission costNetwork gas paid by the public wallet that submits
                NetworkBNB Smart Chain (chain 56 or configured testnet), gas paid in BNB

                Quick start

                From nothing to a private balance in a few minutes.

                1. Create a wallet

                Open Profile and choose New wallet. Write the 24 words down in order and set a password. The words are the wallet; the password only unlocks the copy kept encrypted in this browser. On another device, import the same 24 words.

                2. Connect a public wallet

                Use Connect in the top bar to link OKX Wallet or another browser wallet. It adds BNB to your private balance. Your private balance never sits in it.

                3. Mint

                On Mint, each transaction mints exactly 1 free lot. The actual submitting wallet must hold the membership NFT, may mint at most 10 times and pays network gas only. You can instead create a package without connecting that wallet and submit it later from another device. The {token} arrive as a private note for this wallet, or for any 4041 address entered under To.

                4. Use your balance

                Send, receive and withdraw, and place or fill private limit orders. Choose Submit now to have a connected public wallet pay network gas, or Package only to copy the fixed proof to another device. The submitting wallet cannot change the action bound into the proof.

                Profile lists every private address you have made. Give each payer a new one: addresses cannot be linked to each other.

                Notes

                A note is a private coin: an amount of one asset that belongs to one private address.

                What a note holds

                FieldMeaning
                Asset0 for {token}, 1 for BNB
                ValueA 64-bit amount; BNB is counted in units of 0.00000001
                OwnerDerived from your keys and the address that was paid
                Lock time0 for ordinary notes
                RandomnessMakes every note unique
                MemoUp to 63 bytes, encrypted with the note

                Commitments

                The pool never sees a note, only its commitment, built with the Poseidon2 hash:

                inner = Poseidon2(D_INNER, owner, lockUntil, rcm)
cm    = Poseidon2(D_NOTE, value + asset·2^64, inner)

                A deposit only sends inner. The contract adds the asset and the amount it actually received and computes cm itself, so minting and depositing need no proof.

                The note tree

                Commitments enter an append-only Merkle tree of depth 32, two leaves at a time. The contract remembers every root, so a proof can refer to any earlier state of the tree; the wallet uses the latest one.

                Nullifiers

                Spending a note publishes its nullifier:

                nf = Poseidon2(D_NF, nk, Poseidon2(D_LOC, cm, leafIndex))

                Only the holder of the nullifier key nk can compute it, so whoever paid you cannot tell when you spend. The pool refuses any nullifier it has seen before: that is what prevents double spending.

                Encrypted notes

                Every new note carries a 175-byte ciphertext (ChaCha20-Poly1305 to a one-time key). Your wallet tries each new note on chain and keeps the ones that open and whose commitment matches. Change and other notes you send to yourself use a separate key, so a receive-only view never sees them.

                Open-value notes

                Swap outputs and order payouts are only known when the contract runs. Their ciphertext leaves the amount out; the wallet reads it from the pool's public Shielded event and accepts the note only if the commitment matches.

                Keys and addresses

                24 words make one wallet. One wallet has as many private addresses as you like.

                From words to keys

                The 24 words encode a 32-byte seed. Every key is derived from it with HKDF-SHA256:

                KeyUsed for
                skSpending: proves you own your notes
                nkNullifiers: marks a note spent
                ivkIncoming view: finds payments to any of your addresses
                ovkOutgoing view: encrypts change and notes to yourself

                No key comes from an Ethereum signature, so no website can recreate your wallet by asking you to sign something.

                Private addresses

                An address is 4041… followed by a diversifier d, a public key and an owner value:

                pk_d    = ivk · G(d)                          (Ristretto255)
owner_d = Poseidon2(D_OWNER, spendPub, nkc, d)

                Each d gives a new address. Addresses with different d cannot be linked to each other, yet ivk scans all of them at once.

                The default address uses pm/address/0; New address takes pm/address/1, 2, … in turn, so Profile can list them all again after you restore the 24 words. The wallet checks the first 256 for payments.

                Each address ends with a 4-byte checksum on top of bech32m: a mistyped or cut-off address is refused before anything is sent.

                On this device

                The seed is stored only in this browser, encrypted with your password (scrypt). Proofs are made locally and keys never leave the device. Lock clears them from memory.

                Proofs

                A private transaction is a zero-knowledge proof that you own the notes you spend and that the amounts add up.

                The transfer circuit

                Written in Noir and proved with UltraHonk, it spends two notes and creates two, all of one asset. It shows that:

                • each spent note is in the tree under the given root and is not locked;
                • each nullifier belongs to its note;
                • the new commitments are well formed;
                • inputs equal outputs plus the amount taken out plus the fee.

                Unused slots hold zero-value notes that look the same on chain, so nobody can tell how many inputs and outputs were real or which output is change.

                Public inputs

                InputMeaning
                rootThe tree state the proof refers to
                nf[2]Nullifiers of the two spent notes
                cm[2]Commitments of the two new notes
                nowTime used for lock checks; never later than the block
                asset{token} or BNB
                publicOutAmount leaving the pool (withdraw, swap, order)
                feeZero for wallet-submitted authorization packages
                extHashEverything else the proof is bound to

                What a proof is bound to

                extHash = keccak256(chainId, pool, recipient, relayer,
                    caller, data, ciphertext0, ciphertext1) mod p

                The proof covers the public recipient, allowed submitting contract, contract parameters and both ciphertexts. A gas-paying wallet can submit it but cannot change any bound value or replay it on another chain or pool.

                Proving in the browser

                Proofs are made in your browser with Barretenberg (WebAssembly, multi-threaded). The proving parameters are served by this site and checked against a fixed SHA-256 before use. A proof is 8,000 bytes; the pool verifies it on chain.

                Wallet submission

                The protocol has no transaction relayer. A public wallet pays network gas, while the proof fixes the action.

                Submit now

                Connect any compatible public wallet. It signs the on-chain transaction and pays gas only; it does not receive private keys and cannot change the recipient, amounts, pool or call parameters.

                Package only

                Your private wallet creates a copyable authorization package without submitting it. On any device, open Submit package, inspect the values decoded against the current trusted configuration, connect a public wallet and submit.

                A package contains a proof and fixed call parameters, not a seed or pre-signed nonce transaction. Anyone holding it may submit that fixed action. Deleting the text does not revoke it.

                Requests in flight

                The wallet records exported and submitted actions before they leave the browser. Do not create the payment again while its outcome is unknown.

                Mint

                Every lot lands as a private note.

                Lots21,000
                Per lot1,000 {token} · free on the NFT free-test deployment
                Per transactionExactly 1 lot

                How it works

                For each lot, your wallet prepares a note for a private address and encrypts it; the pool adds the commitment to the tree and counts the lot. The receiving address is never shown, and it can be anyone's. Every lot looks the same on chain: the same amount and the same ciphertext length.

                Free Mint

                Your browser proves the authorized Mint and its private output. The actual submitting public wallet must hold the membership NFT, is limited to 10 mints and pays network gas only. Package-only mode creates the fixed authorization without requiring that wallet until submission.

                On open-submission pools, any eligible public wallet can call the Mint router with the fixed package. The router submits the bound proof to the pool and cannot change its private output. Older wallet-bound Mint pools do not support portable Mint.

                The current pool is explicit; older deployments show their on-chain Mint price and access rules. They require enough funds already present in the selected private balance; this form no longer combines Mint with a public-wallet top-up.

                Deposit and withdraw

                Move funds between a public wallet and your private balance.

                Deposit BNB first

                Send BNB with a deposit transaction from your public wallet; it becomes a BNB note. The depositing wallet pays the network gas.

                Deposit {token}

                A deposit transaction from your public wallet burns the {token} there and creates a private note for the same amount. The wallet pays only network gas in BNB.

                Withdraw

                Enter a public address and an amount. Your browser proves the spend; submit it with a connected public wallet or export a package for another device. The pool pays the whole {token} or BNB amount to the fixed public address.

                PublicHidden
                The public address, asset and amountWhich notes paid or received it

                Send and merge

                Private transfers move value between notes without showing who paid whom.

                Send

                Choose an asset, a 4041 address, an amount and an optional memo. The wallet spends up to two notes, makes one note for the recipient and one for your change, and encrypts each.

                When one note covers the payment, the wallet also folds a smaller loose note into the change, at no extra cost. Fewer notes means larger payments fit in one transaction.

                Merge

                A transaction spends at most two notes. Merge combines your two smallest notes of an asset into one.

                On chain

                PublicHidden
                Time, gas-paying wallet, asset, two nullifiers, two commitments, ciphertextsSender, private recipient, amount, how many inputs and outputs were real

                Market

                Limit orders where the price is public and the trader is not.

                Listings and offers

                A listing sells {token} for BNB; an offer buys {token} with BNB. Prices are quoted per 1,000 {token}.

                Placing an order

                Your proof pays the amount you sell into the market contract and binds the price and a maker. The maker is a one-time order key derived from your seed:

                pm/order-key/v2/<chainId>/<market>/<i>      (secp256k1)

                The maker address is public. The wallet derives order keys from your seed, so the same recovery words can recover your on-chain orders on another device.

                Filling

                Pay with private notes (the proof binds the order and your output note, and you receive a note) or from a public wallet. A fill rounds in the maker's favour and never takes more than what is left.

                Batch buying

                404 Market V2 can buy across up to 20 listings in one transaction, cheapest first. Review each selected order, the total payment, protocol fee and minimum received before submitting or exporting the fixed authorization package. A changed order requires a new review.

                Protocol fees

                The site reads the selected market's on-chain fee; it does not assume all deployments charge the same rate. 404 Market V2 charges both sides of each fill: the payer pays the trade amount plus its fee, and the maker receives the trade amount minus its fee. At 2% per side, a trade amount of 100 costs the payer 102 and credits the maker 98. Older immutable market rates remain unchanged.

                Placing an order and cancelling its unfilled remainder do not incur this fill fee. Claiming proceeds does not charge it again. Network gas is separate.

                Claim and cancel

                The order key signs a typed Release message. A connected public wallet submits it and pays network gas; what is released returns as a private note.

                Minimums

                Amounts must fit the protocol's note units and the selected order's remaining balance. The site checks the current market terms and available notes before review; it does not apply old relayer minimums to wallet-submitted trades.

                Your orders after a restore

                Import the same recovery words and select the same network and market. The wallet checks order-key indices 0–9,999 in batches and matches their maker addresses to on-chain orders, including closed orders. Public maker addresses are cached for the current session to avoid repeating the derivation on every refresh.

                This restores on-chain orders within the 10,000-key range, not unsubmitted packages from another device. Reaching the range limit stops new order creation but does not hide recovered orders or prevent claiming and cancelling them.

                Personal transaction history

                Open Profile to see this wallet's complete recovered chain history and local requests. This includes its private notes and order activity, not the whole pool's or public Gas wallet's transaction feed. The same recovery words recover on-chain records, but a missing local journal cannot reveal old private recipients or intent that was never public. Unknown fields stay unknown; note receipts and spends can include change.

                Public and hidden

                What each action shows on chain, side by side.

                ActionPublicHidden
                Mint, NFT-gatedOne lot, time, submitting wallet and its Mint count, commitment locationThe private address that receives
                SendTime, submitting wallet, asset, nullifiers, commitmentsSender, recipient, amount
                Deposit / WithdrawPublic address, asset, amountWhich note it is in the pool
                SwapAmounts in and out, timeWho swapped, who received
                MarketSize, price, order key, each fillWho placed or filled it, who received

                Getting the most from it

                • Privacy starts when a note is spent, and it grows with the number of people using the pool.
                • Give each payer a new address.
                • Move fresh mints and deposits after some other activity.
                • Pick amounts that do not equal a whole number of lots or a public deposit. The wallet points it out when one does.

                Sync and recovery

                Your balance is rebuilt from public chain data and your keys alone.

                Sync

                The wallet downloads the pool's NoteAdded, Nullified, Transacted and Shielded events, rebuilds the tree locally and tries every new note. The pool keeps a public list of blocks with activity, so only those blocks are fetched. No server is ever asked for a balance or a note.

                Checks

                After each sync the wallet compares its tree root, nullifier count, nullifier digest and transaction digest with the contract at the same block. If anything differs, it rebuilds from the deployment block.

                Recovery

                The 24 words and the chain bring back every note, your numbered addresses and your orders. Requests in flight are saved on the device, encrypted with a key derived from the seed for this chain and pool.

                Contracts

                On BNB Smart Chain (chain 56 by default; test deployments use chain 97). No upgrades, and no admin key that can move funds.

                ContractAddress

                Supply checks

                Two equalities hold at every block, and every withdrawal is limited by its asset's balance in the pool:

                {token}:  totalSupply + poolBalance[{token}] = mintedLots × LOT
BNB: pool balance = poolBalance[BNB] × NATIVE_UNIT + mintProceeds
